newsitem.title: USA: Case sees Q3 oper income up eight pct.
newsitem.headline: Case sees Q3 oper income up eight pct.

text.p: Case Corp said on Wednesday that it expects to report 1996 third quarter operating income up eight percent from the $95 million reported a year ago.
The year ago figure excludes a one-time gain of $24 million from the sale of its Viscosity Oil unit.
The company also expects to meet the First Call consensus of $0.78 a share when it reports earnings on Thursday morning.
"We intend to meet that expectation," chief executive officer Jean-Pierre Rosso said in a telephone interview.

The Racine, Wisconsin-based farm equipment and construction machinery maker reported third quarter earnings of $1.19 a share a year ago. That figure included several special items, including a one-time gain and a higher 1996 tax rate, Case said.
Rosso added that the operating earnings comparison was a more direct comparison than the per share figures, due to special factors in 1995's earnings and a change in the company's tax rate.
Sales for the quarter should be flat compared with the $1.14 billion reported a year ago, as a result of Case's push to reduce inventories in its supply chain to dealers.
"The reason we grew operating earnings in a flat sales environment is because of our cost reduction, which continued to produce results," Rosso said.
